supersedes.note: BD-150: build-release.ps1 stamps DriverVer = driver_date,<-DriverVer> and refuses a package that does not rank above this release's DriverVer, because PnP keeps the installed package on an equal date and version.

mft_h264.note: The H.264 encoder Media Foundation transform (M15.11). register true: the installer copies payload/mft/amdgpu_wddm_mft_h264.dll to <install root>\mft\ and writes route A of driver/umd/mft-h264/INSTALL.md machine wide. register false: the installer installs and registers nothing, and takes away what an earlier install of this release family wrote. The value travels into manifest.json, so the package itself says what it does. This is the bisect lever of the encoder wagon.

opengl_icd.note: The OpenGL installable client driver (BD-076, GitHub issue #8). register true: the installer copies payload/opengl/amdgpu_wddm_gl.dll to <install root>\opengl\ and writes the three values OpenGLDriverName, OpenGLVersion and OpenGLFlags into the GPU's own software key, where Windows' opengl32.dll reads them through D3DKMTQueryAdapterInfo(KMTQAITYPE_UMOPENGLINFO). Every 64-bit OpenGL application of the computer then runs on the GPU, with no DLL beside its executable. architectures is the list of the architectures this release registers, and it is x64 alone. The reason is measured: on unit A, 2026-10-12 13:05-13:08Z, the x64 ICD passed every case of tools/win/gltest (core 4.6, renderer "zink Vulkan 1.4(AMD BC-250 (RADV GFX1013) (MESA_RADV))", draw, present, threads and compute exact), and the x86 ICD failed every case with one debug string from the loaded DLL, "MESA: error: ZINK: failed to load vulkan-1.dll": this computer has no 32-bit Vulkan loader, so zink has no Vulkan to run on. The 32-bit half of the registration itself was correct down to the kernel answer (glprobe: the kernel named the x86 file, version 1, flags 0x1, opengl32 mapped it and DrvValidateVersion returned TRUE), so a 32-bit registration would only trade the Windows software renderer, which is OpenGL 1.1 but draws, for an ICD that gives a 32-bit program no context at all. A later release that ships a 32-bit Vulkan loader adds "x86" to this list and the files row of the x86 build, and nothing else changes: the installer, the gates and the tests all work from the list. register false: the installer registers nothing and takes away the values and the files of an earlier install of this release family; an architecture that leaves the list is taken away the same way by an install that registers the others. The value travels into manifest.json, so the package itself says what it does, and it is the bisect lever of the OpenGL wagon. With register true the build refuses a package that does not carry the file of every architecture of the list, and the files row of this file names the built ICD with its SHA256 and its provenance; docs/testing/THIRD-PARTY.md carries a row for it (the build refuses a payload file without one). The file is still unpublished: tools/release/provenance.py refuses a payload file whose build commit or recipe commit no remote-tracking branch contains, so the Mesa commit of amdgpu-wddm/bd076-wgl-icd and the recipe commit of install/bd076-opengl-icd have to be pushed before a package can be cut. value_type REG_MULTI_SZ is what every shipping WDDM display INF writes for this value and what this installer writes for UserModeDriverName; REG_SZ is the fallback the 2021 Learn table describes. A bare file name without a directory is not a step in between: the install root is not on the loader search path of an arbitrary application, so nothing would find the file. version 1 is the number the runtime validates (Mesa's WGL front end ignores it); flags 1 sets bit 0 only, so the runtime keeps its finish call before every swap-buffers call.

The Win32 semaphore line: an import keeps an owned duplicate, as the Vulkan specification requires, instead of taking the application's NT handle away from it; an export applies the access mask, the inherit flag and the name the application asked for; and a named import maps Global and Local to the BaseNamedObjects paths. Audit finding A5/UMD-2: DeviceLease::Take returns an HRESULT and the transform runs nothing without the lease. It passed nullptr for the device output of IMFDXGIDeviceManager::LockDevice and dropped the status of both OpenDeviceHandle and LockDevice, so a client that reset its device manager let our dispatches and the client's own work reach one device context at once while the transform reported success. S_OK now means the lease is held, or that there is no manager at all and the transform owns its device; a lock that writes no device is E_UNEXPECTED, and the device the manager hands back is kept for the life of the lease and released before the unlock. Audit finding A11/UMD-3: the dependency-safe Waves deblock schedule is the default again. The Rows schedule is one dispatch whose forward progress rests on all macroblock-row groups being resident at once, which Direct3D does not promise; when its spin budget ran out a group filtered anyway and published the same count an ordered row publishes, so the reconstruction drifted with no failure word anywhere. Waves synchronises at the dispatch boundary and assumes no residency, its order is arithmetic a test can read (DeblockWaveRows/DeblockWaveCount), and BC250_MFT_DEBLOCK=rows selects the single dispatch explicitly Carried from 0.7.216.100-tester.24: bc250-win 689852a8 (train/b20-setup), which carries e52/encoder-perf e4d1f630, the H.264 encoder transform; the respin does not rebuild it

The file is the same build in the D3D12, D3D11 and 32-bit Vulkan slots, as before. Built with the radv-mt set, /Brepro, from a clean work tree at that commit. files.role: OpenGL ICD for 64-bit applications (BD-076, GitHub issue #8): Mesa's gallium WGL target built on zink and renamed amdgpu_wddm_gl.dll, so Windows' own opengl32.dll loads it as the adapter's installable client driver and every 64-bit OpenGL application of the computer renders on the GPU with no DLL beside its executable. It exports the 19 Drv entry points of the contract (gallium_wgl.def of the build, staged next to the file); DrvSwapMultipleBuffers is not one of them and the runtime does not need it. Static CRT and b_ndebug, because this file loads into foreign processes. opengl_icd.register of this file governs the registration and opengl_icd.architectures which architectures get it; this release registers x64 alone, so there is no x86 row, and a 32-bit OpenGL program keeps the software renderer of Windows itself. BD-167, release flavour: rebuilt at mesa fork fix/bd167-release-gl 71b34d2c, the published head of this line, which is the BD-076 ICD commit 9fa76f54 with the ten release-flavour commits of the OpenGL line on top. The image holds none of the fifteen override names the declaration demands of its lab copy: the MESA_ dump, cache, read and override paths, ZINK_DEBUG, GALLIUM_DRIVER, LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE, D3D_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE and XDG_CACHE_HOME.
